newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's of London sets up Japanese service company.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's of London sets up Japanese service company.

text.p: Lloyd's of London said on Friday that its market board had approved the formation of Lloyd's Japan Inc, a Tokyo-based service company which will be a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Corporation of Lloyd's.

Richard Keeling, chairman of the Murray Lawrence group and of Lloyd's Japan steering group, said this marked "further important steps in the establishment of the Society's direct insurance business in Japan".

He said that over the next few weeks Lloyd's underwriters would be able to participate formally as co-investors in Lloyd's Japan Inc, which would facilitate the marketing, development and administration of Lloyd's underwriters' direct insurance business in Japan.
"Underwriters who participate will enjoy ten years' exclusive access to the Society's Japanese insurance licences," Keeling added.
Lloyd's applications for licences are currently being considered by Japan's Ministry of Finance, Lloyd's said.
The insurance market also said Jason Light had been appointed as managing director Lloyd's Japan, based in London.
